description: Twelve-channel macro controller: a keyframe stores the levels of all twelve VCAs at one point on a timeline, and the large knob moves along that timeline, interpolating between the keyframes

params.text: Chooses which channels the AMP knob edits, and clicking it moves the selection scope on to the next of one channel, a column of two, and all twelve
Sets the level of the channels in the selection scope at the current keyframe, and clicking it flips those channels between their lowest and highest levels
Moves along the timeline, interpolating levels between the keyframes on either side; VCA levels can be edited only while it points at a keyframe
Inverts the levels of the channels in the selection scope at the current keyframe, and pressing it again puts them back
Adds a keyframe at the current timeline position, or deletes the keyframe already there
Normals an internal 10V offset to every channel input with nothing patched, so those channels generate control voltages instead of passing an external signal
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the MOD input before it moves the timeline, and at the centre no modulation gets through

inputs.text: Audio or control voltage into that channel's VCA; each odd-numbered input is normalled to the even-numbered input beside it, so one cable fills a stereo pair
Moves the timeline, added to the position of the large knob and scaled by the MOD attenuator; in the two sequencer modes a trigger here moves to the next keyframe

outputs.text: That channel's input after its VCA, and patching it subtracts that channel from the mix output for its row
A 10ms trigger each time a keyframe becomes active
The mix of the odd-numbered channel outputs, without any channel whose own output jack is patched
The mix of the even-numbered channel outputs, without any channel whose own output jack is patched

notes: the maker's manual says at least two keyframes are needed before there is anything to interpolate; turn the timeline knob to a position, press KEY, move to another position and press KEY again
the AMP knob changes nothing while the timeline knob points between keyframes; move it onto a keyframe, or add one with KEY, before editing levels
menu: Selection scope — chooses Single, Columns or All for which channels the AMP knob edits
Sequencing mode — chooses Keyframer, which interpolates between keyframes, Sequencer (step), which moves on one keyframe at a trigger, or Sequencer (random)
Interpolation curve — chooses Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic, Sine, Step A or Step B for how the selected channels travel between keyframes
VCA response — chooses Linear, 25%, 50%, 75% or Exponential for how the level of the selected channels follows the AMP knob
Copy keyframe — takes the levels of the keyframe at the timeline position now, and Paste keyframe writes them at whatever position is reached next
Randomize levels — gives every channel in the selection scope a new random level at the current keyframe
Delete all keyframes — empties the timeline and returns every channel to linear interpolation and linear response
Factory presets — a submenu of twelve worked examples, from Null (no keyframes) and Min/max fader through the submixes and crossfaders to Six CV/gate sequencers
Toggle min/max levels — flips the channels in the selection scope between their lowest and highest levels, which is what clicking the AMP knob does
Invert levels — inverts the levels of the channels in the selection scope, which is what the VAR button does
